questions.scenario: A developer needs a Lambda function to process a Kinesis stream with higher throughput without adding shards. Which event source mapping setting should be increased?
questions.explain: ParallelizationFactor allows up to 10 concurrent batches per shard, multiplying throughput without changing shard count, while still preserving order within each partition key. BatchSize changes records per invocation but not concurrency. MaximumRetryAttempts controls failure handling, and StartingPosition sets where reading begins.

questions.scenario: An application must store a shopping cart that expires 24 hours after the last update, with minimal cost and no cleanup code. Which combination should be used?
options: DynamoDB with a TTL attribute updated on each write
DynamoDB with a scheduled Lambda that scans and deletes
questions.explain: DynamoDB TTL deletes items automatically once the timestamp passes and consumes no write capacity, so refreshing the attribute on each update gives a rolling 24-hour expiry for free. Scheduled scans consume significant capacity, S3 versioning has no expiry semantics of this kind, and an RDS cron job means managing a database and a scheduler.

questions.scenario: Which approach ensures a Lambda function invoked by API Gateway returns a proper CORS response to a browser?
options: Return Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers in the function response and enable CORS on the API
questions.explain: With proxy integration the function must include CORS headers in its response, and the API must handle the preflight OPTIONS request — enabling CORS in API Gateway configures that. Timeouts, authorizers and caching are unrelated to the browser's cross-origin checks.

questions.scenario: An application must guarantee that only one Lambda invocation processes a given order ID even if the event is delivered twice. Which approach is MOST reliable?
options: A conditional DynamoDB write on the order ID that fails if already processed
questions.explain: A conditional put using attribute_not_exists on the order ID succeeds exactly once, making duplicate deliveries harmless — the standard idempotency pattern. Concurrency of 1 serialises processing but a duplicate would still be processed twice, and timeout settings only change timing rather than preventing duplicates.

questions.scenario: Which TWO characteristics distinguish Amazon SQS from Amazon SNS?
options: SQS stores messages until a consumer retrieves and deletes them
SNS pushes each message to all subscribers immediately
SQS pushes messages to multiple subscribers automatically
SNS stores messages for up to 14 days
SQS guarantees delivery to every subscriber
questions.explain: SQS is pull-based: messages persist in the queue until a consumer receives and deletes them, and each message is processed by one consumer. SNS is push-based: it delivers each published message to all current subscribers immediately and does not durably store messages for offline subscribers, which is why SNS is often paired with SQS.

questions.scenario: Which DynamoDB operation should be used to increment a counter atomically without reading the item first?
options: UpdateItem with an ADD or SET expression using a numeric increment
questions.explain: UpdateItem with an atomic counter expression such as SET count = count + :inc applies the increment server-side, so concurrent updates do not lose writes. Read-then-write introduces a race where two clients read the same value and one overwrites the other. BatchWriteItem replaces items, and scanning first is wasteful.

questions.scenario: A developer must send a message to an SQS FIFO queue and prevent duplicates of the same content within five minutes. Which mechanism handles this?
options: Content-based deduplication or an explicit MessageDeduplicationId
questions.explain: FIFO queues deduplicate using a MessageDeduplicationId, either provided explicitly or derived from a SHA-256 of the body when content-based deduplication is enabled, within a five-minute window. MessageGroupId controls ordering and parallelism, while visibility timeout and delay affect delivery timing.

questions.scenario: An application must trigger different Lambda functions depending on whether an EventBridge event's detail-type is OrderPlaced or OrderCancelled. What is the cleanest design?
options: Two rules on the same event bus, each with an event pattern matching one detail-type
One rule targeting a router Lambda that inspects and re-invokes
A scheduled rule polling a database
questions.explain: EventBridge rules filter on event content, so one rule per detail-type routes directly to the correct target with no custom routing code and no extra invocation cost. A router function adds latency, cost and a failure point. Separate buses complicate publishing, and polling abandons event-driven design.

questions.scenario: Which storage class should be used for objects accessed roughly once per quarter that must be retrieved within milliseconds when needed?
questions.explain: Glacier Instant Retrieval targets rarely accessed data that still requires millisecond retrieval, at far lower storage cost than Standard. Standard is priced for frequent access, Deep Archive retrieval takes hours, and Express One Zone is a high-performance class for very frequently accessed data in a single availability zone.

questions.scenario: A Lambda function must call an external HTTPS API that rate-limits to 10 requests per second. Which approach protects the external API?
options: Buffer requests through SQS and set reserved concurrency to limit the invocation rate
questions.explain: Queuing decouples arrival rate from processing rate, and reserved concurrency caps how many invocations run simultaneously, holding the outbound call rate within the external limit. More memory, provisioned concurrency and longer timeouts all leave the request rate unchanged or make it worse.

questions.scenario: Which statement about the AWS SDK's default behaviour for DynamoDB reads is correct?
options: Reads are eventually consistent unless ConsistentRead is set to true
questions.explain: DynamoDB reads default to eventually consistent, costing half an RCU per 4 KB; strong consistency must be requested explicitly with ConsistentRead and costs a full RCU. DAX is used only when the application connects through a DAX cluster, and all reads consume capacity.

questions.scenario: An application must process files uploaded to S3 and the processing must not start until the entire multipart upload has completed. Which event type should trigger the function?
questions.explain: CompleteMultipartUpload fires only when all parts have been assembled into the final object, so processing never sees a partial upload; the wildcard s3:ObjectCreated:* also covers it. Post covers browser form uploads, and the removal and restore events relate to deletion and Glacier retrieval.

questions.scenario: Which service should be used to run a containerised batch job that needs 32 GB of memory for two hours, with no cluster management?
questions.explain: AWS Batch schedules containerised jobs and can run them on Fargate, handling queueing and provisioning with no cluster to manage, and supports large memory allocations and long runtimes. Lambda caps at 15 minutes and 10 GB of memory. Manual EC2 scheduling means managing infrastructure, and API Gateway is not a compute service.

questions.scenario: A developer must reduce the number of DynamoDB read operations for a query whose results change at most once per hour. What is the simplest effective change?
options: Cache the query result in the application or in ElastiCache with a one-hour TTL
questions.explain: Caching results with a TTL matching the change frequency eliminates almost all repeated reads. Strongly consistent reads double read cost, an LSI serves alternative query patterns rather than reducing read volume, and write capacity does not affect reads.

questions.scenario: Which HTTP method should an idempotent update to an existing resource use in a REST API?
questions.explain: PUT replaces a resource with the supplied representation, so repeating the same request produces the same final state — it is idempotent by definition. POST creates a new subordinate resource each time and is not idempotent. PATCH can be idempotent but depends on the patch semantics, and CONNECT establishes tunnels.

questions.scenario: An application must retrieve 200 items from DynamoDB by their primary keys in as few calls as possible. Which operation should be used?
options: BatchGetItem in pages of up to 100 items
questions.explain: BatchGetItem retrieves up to 100 items (or 16 MB) per call, so 200 keys take two calls instead of 200 round trips. Looping GetItem is far slower, Scan reads the entire table, and Query requires a partition key condition and cannot fetch arbitrary unrelated keys.

questions.scenario: Which approach allows a Lambda function to be triggered by an Application Load Balancer?
options: Register the function as a target in a Lambda target group
Attach the function to the ALB security group
Add the function to an Auto Scaling group
Create a VPC endpoint for Lambda
questions.explain: ALB supports Lambda targets: the function is registered in a target group of type lambda and receives a specific event format, returning a response with statusCode and body. Security groups control network access, Auto Scaling groups manage EC2 instances, and a VPC endpoint provides private API access rather than an invocation path.

questions.scenario: A developer must keep a DynamoDB table synchronised to an OpenSearch domain for full-text search. What is the recommended pattern?
options: DynamoDB Streams triggering a Lambda function that indexes documents in OpenSearch
A nightly Scan of the whole table
questions.explain: Streams deliver every change in near real time and a Lambda consumer keeps the search index current with minimal lag and cost. A nightly Scan is expensive and leaves the index stale all day, manual exports are neither timely nor automated, and DAX is a read cache with no search capability.

questions.scenario: Which setting controls how many messages a Lambda function receives per invocation from an SQS event source?
questions.explain: BatchSize on the event source mapping determines how many messages are delivered in each invocation, up to 10 for standard queues (or more with a batching window). Visibility timeout governs redelivery, maximum message size limits payload bytes, and delay seconds postpones initial availability.

questions.scenario: An application must generate a unique, sortable identifier for records inserted at high rate across many nodes. Which approach is MOST suitable?
options: A time-ordered identifier such as ULID or KSUID generated client-side
An auto-incrementing integer from a single counter row
A random UUIDv4 used as a sort key for ordering
The current second as the primary key
questions.explain: Time-ordered identifiers embed a timestamp so they sort chronologically while remaining unique across nodes without coordination. A single counter row is a contention bottleneck and single point of failure, UUIDv4 is unique but not sortable by time, and second-based keys collide heavily and create hot partitions.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service provides an in-memory data store that supports sorted sets, pub/sub and Lua scripting?
questions.explain: Redis supports rich data structures including sorted sets, plus pub/sub, transactions, Lua scripting and persistence. Memcached provides only simple key-value caching with no such features. DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL database rather than an in-memory store, and Neptune is a graph database.

questions.scenario: An application must allow a user to access AWS resources after authenticating with a corporate SAML identity provider. Which service enables this for AWS API access?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center or IAM SAML federation with AssumeRoleWithSAML
questions.explain: IAM Identity Center or IAM SAML federation exchanges a SAML assertion for temporary AWS credentials via AssumeRoleWithSAML, which is the standard workforce federation path. Cognito user pools target application end users, Secrets Manager stores secrets, and Macie discovers sensitive data.

questions.scenario: Which statement about S3 bucket policies versus IAM policies for cross-account access is correct?
options: Both the bucket policy in the resource account and an identity policy in the caller account must allow the action
Only the bucket policy is required
Only the identity policy is required
Neither is required if the bucket is encrypted
questions.explain: Cross-account access requires an allow on both sides: the resource owner grants access in the bucket policy, and the caller's account grants permission in an identity policy. Within a single account either policy alone suffices. Encryption is orthogonal to authorisation and grants nothing.

questions.scenario: A developer must ensure a KMS key can only be used by a specific Lambda function. Which condition is MOST appropriate in the key policy?
options: A condition restricting use to the function's execution role ARN
No condition, granting the whole account
questions.explain: Scoping the key policy to the execution role's ARN ensures only that function can use the key, following least privilege. Source IP is meaningless for a managed service with dynamic addresses, time conditions restrict when rather than who, and granting the whole account allows every principal in it.

questions.scenario: Which mechanism prevents an application from accepting an expired Cognito access token?
options: Validating the exp claim during token verification
questions.explain: Token verification must check the exp (expiry) claim along with the signature, issuer and audience; a token past its expiry must be rejected. Length reveals nothing, storage location does not affect validity, and refreshing on every request defeats the purpose of short-lived access tokens without validating anything.

questions.scenario: Which TWO practices reduce the risk of secrets leaking through a CI/CD pipeline?
options: Retrieve secrets at runtime from Secrets Manager rather than storing them in the pipeline
Mask or suppress secret values in build logs
Print secrets to the build log for debugging
Commit a .env file so all builds share the same values
Email secrets to the team for convenience
questions.explain: Fetching secrets at runtime keeps them out of pipeline configuration and source control, and masking prevents accidental exposure in build output that many people can read. Printing secrets, committing them to a repository and emailing them all create durable copies in places that are hard to revoke.

questions.scenario: Which service protects a public web application from common exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting at the edge?
questions.explain: AWS WAF inspects HTTP requests and blocks those matching rules for SQL injection, XSS, rate limits and custom patterns, and attaches to CloudFront, ALB and API Gateway. Shield Standard defends against network and transport layer DDoS, Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities, and Config evaluates resource configuration compliance.

questions.scenario: An application must ensure that data written to an S3 bucket is encrypted even if the client omits encryption headers. What should be enabled?
questions.explain: Default bucket encryption applies server-side encryption automatically to objects uploaded without explicit encryption headers, so nothing lands unencrypted. Object Lock enforces retention, Requester Pays shifts billing, and Transfer Acceleration optimises upload paths.

questions.scenario: Which is the correct way to allow an EC2 instance to read a specific Secrets Manager secret?
options: Attach an instance profile whose role allows secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on that secret ARN
Store the secret in user data
Grant the role secretsmanager:* on all secrets
questions.explain: An instance role scoped to GetSecretValue on the specific secret ARN follows least privilege while providing temporary credentials automatically. User data is visible via instance metadata and is not a secret store, wildcard access over all secrets is excessive, and secrets can never be safely public.

questions.scenario: Which statement describes the correct handling of an AccessDeniedException returned by an AWS SDK call?
options: It indicates missing or insufficient IAM permissions for that action or resource
It indicates the service is unavailable and should be retried
It indicates the request payload was too large
questions.explain: AccessDenied is an authorisation failure, meaning the principal lacks permission for the action or resource, or an explicit deny applies — retrying will not help and the policy must be corrected. Service unavailability returns 5xx errors, timeouts surface as connection errors, and oversized payloads produce specific size-related errors.

questions.scenario: A developer must ensure that only encrypted connections are accepted by an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL database. What should be configured?
options: Set the rds.force_ssl parameter to 1 in the parameter group
questions.explain: Setting rds.force_ssl to 1 makes the database reject any non-TLS connection attempt, enforcing encryption in transit at the server. Backups protect durability, Multi-AZ provides availability, and instance size affects performance — none of which enforce TLS.

questions.scenario: Which approach should be used to store a private key that an application needs to sign requests?
options: AWS KMS with an asymmetric key, keeping the private key inside KMS
A plaintext file in the deployment package
questions.explain: An asymmetric KMS key never exposes the private key material — the application calls kms:Sign and KMS performs the operation internally, so the key cannot be exfiltrated. Files in packages, plaintext environment variables and public objects all place the private key where it can be copied.

questions.scenario: Which IAM feature allows testing whether a policy grants a specific action before deploying it?
questions.explain: The IAM policy simulator evaluates policies against specified actions and resources and reports allow or deny with the deciding statement, letting you validate changes safely. CloudTrail Insights detects unusual API activity after the fact, Config assesses resource compliance, and Trusted Advisor gives general best-practice checks.

questions.scenario: An API must reject requests whose body exceeds an expected schema, before invoking the backend. What should be configured in API Gateway?
options: Request validation against a JSON Schema model
questions.explain: Request validators check the body against a JSON Schema model and reject non-conforming requests with 400 before any integration is invoked, saving cost and reducing attack surface. Usage plans throttle, stage variables carry configuration, and gateway responses customise error output.

questions.scenario: Which is true about IAM permission boundaries?
options: They set the maximum permissions an identity-based policy can grant to a principal
They apply only to resource-based policies
They replace the need for identity policies
questions.explain: A permission boundary caps the effective permissions of a user or role: the principal can only do what both its identity policy and the boundary allow. Boundaries never grant permissions on their own, apply to IAM principals rather than resource policies, and do not remove the need for identity policies.

questions.scenario: Which approach ensures that logs written by a Lambda function cannot be modified or deleted by the function's own role?
options: Grant only logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents, not delete permissions
Store logs in the function's /tmp directory
questions.explain: Granting only the create-stream and put-events actions lets the function append logs while denying any ability to delete or alter them, preserving the audit trail. Wildcard logs permissions would allow deletion, disabling logging removes the trail entirely, and /tmp is ephemeral and vanishes with the environment.

questions.scenario: A company must rotate an RDS master password without application downtime. Which Secrets Manager rotation strategy supports this?
options: The alternating users strategy, which maintains two users and switches between them
Storing two passwords in one secret with no rotation function
questions.explain: The alternating users strategy keeps two database users and rotates one while the other remains active, so in-flight connections and applications caching the previous value keep working — this is the zero-downtime approach. Recreating the database causes an outage, and rare or manual rotation does not address downtime at all.

questions.scenario: Which statement about encrypting an existing unencrypted DynamoDB table is correct?
options: DynamoDB encrypts all tables at rest by default and the key type can be changed
Encryption must be enabled at creation and can never change
DynamoDB does not support encryption at rest
questions.explain: All DynamoDB tables are encrypted at rest by default, and the key can be switched between an AWS owned key, an AWS managed key and a customer managed key. There is therefore no such thing as an unencrypted DynamoDB table, and encryption is not limited to global tables.

questions.scenario: A developer must ensure that a CodeBuild project can pull a private base image from Amazon ECR. What is required?
options: The CodeBuild service role needs ECR pull permissions, and the repository policy must allow it
The image must be made public
The image must be copied into S3
questions.explain: CodeBuild authenticates using its service role, so that role needs ecr:GetAuthorizationToken and image pull permissions, and the repository policy must permit the principal. Making images public is a security risk, CodeBuild is fully managed rather than run on your EC2 instances, and S3 is not a container registry.

questions.scenario: Which CloudFormation function retrieves an attribute such as the ARN of a resource created in the same template?
questions.explain: Fn::GetAtt returns a named attribute of a resource, such as Arn or DomainName. Ref returns the resource's default identifier, which varies by type and is not always the ARN. Fn::Select picks an item from a list, and Fn::Split divides a string into a list.

questions.scenario: An application deployed by CodeDeploy to EC2 must stop the running service before new files are copied. Which lifecycle hook should be used?
questions.explain: ApplicationStop runs at the very start of a deployment, before files are copied, and is the correct place to stop the running service gracefully. AfterInstall runs once files are in place, ValidateService verifies the deployment at the end, and BeforeAllowTraffic is a Lambda and ECS hook.

questions.scenario: Which practice makes a CloudFormation template reusable across environments?
options: Parameterise environment-specific values and use Mappings or Conditions
Create a separate template per environment
Use random names generated at deploy time only
questions.explain: Parameters supply per-environment values at deploy time, while Mappings and Conditions adapt behaviour without duplicating templates, keeping one source of truth. Hard-coded names cause collisions and prevent reuse, separate templates drift apart, and purely random names make resources hard to identify.

questions.scenario: A team must roll back a Lambda deployment instantly if a post-deployment validation fails. Which CodeDeploy hook enables automated validation?
options: AfterAllowTraffic running a validation Lambda that can fail the deployment
questions.explain: AfterAllowTraffic runs a validation function once traffic has shifted; if it reports failure, CodeDeploy rolls back automatically to the previous version. ApplicationStart, BeforeInstall and DownloadBundle are EC2 and on-premises lifecycle events, not Lambda hooks.

questions.scenario: Which statement about AWS SAM's implicit resources is correct?
options: Defining an Api event on a function implicitly creates an API Gateway API if none is declared
SAM never creates resources beyond those declared
SAM requires a separate CloudFormation template for API Gateway
questions.explain: SAM creates an implicit AWS::Serverless::Api when a function declares Api events without referencing an explicit API, and its settings can be customised through the Globals section or by declaring the API explicitly. SAM transforms shorthand into many underlying resources, and no separate template is needed.

questions.scenario: Which TWO CodePipeline action types can be used to deploy an application?
options: A CloudFormation deploy action creating or updating a stack
A CodeDeploy action deploying to EC2, Lambda or ECS
A CodeBuild action running unit tests
questions.explain: CloudFormation deploy actions provision or update infrastructure stacks, and CodeDeploy actions deploy application revisions to compute targets — both are deployment actions. Source actions retrieve code, approval actions gate progression, and build actions compile and test rather than deploy.

questions.scenario: A developer must ensure a new ECS task definition revision is used without changing the service definition each time. What should be referenced?
options: The task definition family, allowing ECS to use the latest active revision
questions.explain: Referencing the family lets ECS resolve to the latest active revision, so deployments pick up new revisions automatically. Pinning a revision number requires editing the service on every release. An image digest identifies the image but not the task configuration, and the cluster ARN identifies where tasks run.

questions.scenario: Which Elastic Beanstalk deployment policy briefly runs both old and new application versions on the same instances?
questions.explain: Rolling updates instances in batches, so while a batch is being updated the remaining instances still run the previous version and both serve traffic simultaneously. Immutable and blue/green isolate versions on separate instances or environments, and all at once replaces everything with a brief outage.

questions.scenario: What is the recommended way to store environment-specific configuration for a containerised application on ECS?
options: Reference Systems Manager Parameter Store or Secrets Manager values in the task definition
Bake values into the container image
Use a different Dockerfile per environment
Store values in the ECS cluster name
questions.explain: ECS task definitions can inject values from Parameter Store or Secrets Manager at container start, keeping one image usable across environments and secrets out of the image. Baking values in requires rebuilding per environment and risks leaking secrets, and cluster names are identifiers rather than configuration.

questions.scenario: Which CloudFormation capability must be acknowledged when a template creates IAM resources?
questions.explain: Creating IAM resources requires explicitly acknowledging CAPABILITY_IAM, or CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM when those resources have custom names, so privilege escalation cannot happen silently. CAPABILITY_AUTO_EXPAND applies to macros and transforms such as SAM, and resource policy capability covers a different set of resources.

questions.scenario: A developer wants a pipeline to run automatically whenever code is pushed to the main branch. What should be configured?
options: A source action with change detection, for example an EventBridge rule on the repository
A CloudWatch alarm on the repository size
questions.explain: Change detection via EventBridge starts the pipeline within seconds of a push, which is the point of continuous integration. A daily schedule delays feedback dramatically, manual starts are unreliable, and repository size alarms have nothing to do with commits.

questions.scenario: Which approach allows testing a new API version without affecting existing clients?
options: Deploy the new version to a separate stage or use a canary release on the stage
questions.explain: A separate stage gives the new version its own URL for testing, while API Gateway canary releases route a small percentage of production traffic to the new deployment for safe validation. Overwriting production or deleting the old API breaks existing clients, and disabling authorisation is a security regression.

questions.scenario: What happens when a CloudFormation stack creation fails and rollback is enabled?
options: All resources created during the failed operation are deleted and the stack ends in ROLLBACK_COMPLETE
questions.explain: On a failed create with rollback enabled, CloudFormation deletes the resources it created so no partial infrastructure is left behind, ending in ROLLBACK_COMPLETE — a state from which the stack must be deleted before retrying. It does not retry indefinitely, and nothing locks the account.

questions.scenario: Which practice ensures a deployment can be rolled back quickly if a database migration is involved?
options: Make migrations backward compatible so the previous application version still works
Drop old columns in the same release that stops using them
Run migrations only after the new code is fully deployed everywhere
questions.explain: Backward-compatible (expand-then-contract) migrations let the old and new application versions run against the same schema, so rolling back code does not require rolling back the database. Dropping columns immediately makes rollback impossible, and deferring or avoiding migrations does not address compatibility.

questions.scenario: Which CloudWatch metric statistic is MOST appropriate for detecting occasional slow requests that affect a small fraction of users?
questions.explain: Percentiles such as p99 expose the tail of the distribution where a small fraction of users experience slow responses, which averages hide entirely. Minimum latency shows the best case, and a sum of invocations counts traffic rather than measuring speed.

questions.scenario: An application shows increased errors immediately after a deployment. Which is the FASTEST way to confirm the deployment is the cause?
options: Correlate the error rate metric with the deployment time and roll back to compare
Add more memory to the function
questions.explain: Overlaying the error metric with the deployment timestamp shows whether the increase begins exactly at release, and rolling back confirms causation immediately while restoring service. Retention, memory and alarm deletion do not test the hypothesis, and removing alarms actively reduces visibility.

questions.scenario: Which technique reduces the payload size returned by an API to improve client performance?
options: Enable content encoding such as gzip compression on the API
questions.explain: API Gateway can compress responses when the client advertises support, substantially reducing bytes transferred and improving perceived performance. Timeouts affect how long a request may take, extra parameters do not shrink responses, and disabling caching increases both latency and backend load.

questions.scenario: A developer must determine whether a performance problem is in the application code or in a downstream AWS service. Which X-Ray view helps MOST?
options: The trace timeline showing segment and subsegment durations
questions.explain: The trace timeline breaks a request into segments and subsegments with durations, showing directly whether time is spent in your own code or waiting on a downstream call. Billing dashboards, credential reports and S3 inventories address cost, security posture and object listings respectively.

questions.scenario: Which configuration reduces the number of Lambda invocations when processing a high-volume SQS queue?
options: Increase the batch size and configure a batching window
questions.explain: A larger batch size processes more messages per invocation and a batching window lets Lambda wait briefly to fill batches, cutting invocation count and cost. A batch size of 1 maximises invocations, disabling long polling increases empty receives, and memory does not affect batching.

questions.scenario: An application's CloudWatch alarm fires constantly due to brief metric spikes. What should be adjusted?
options: Increase the number of evaluation periods or datapoints required to alarm
Reduce the metric period to one second
questions.explain: Requiring the threshold to be breached across several evaluation periods filters out transient spikes while still catching sustained problems. Deleting the alarm removes monitoring, lowering the threshold makes it fire more often, and a finer period increases sensitivity to noise.

questions.scenario: Which is the MOST likely cause of a Lambda function reporting 'Task timed out after 3.00 seconds'?
options: The function's configured timeout is lower than the work it performs
The function has too much memory
The IAM role is missing logs permissions
The deployment package is too small
questions.explain: That message means execution reached the configured timeout, which defaults to 3 seconds, so either the timeout must be raised or the work made faster. Excess memory makes functions faster rather than slower, missing log permissions would prevent logs appearing at all, and package size does not cause timeouts.

questions.scenario: A team wants to compare application performance before and after a change using consistent measurements. What should be implemented?
options: Custom CloudWatch metrics emitted for key operations, tracked over time
questions.explain: Custom metrics provide consistent, comparable time series across releases, enabling objective before-and-after analysis and alerting. Manual timing is inconsistent and unrepeatable, screenshots are not analysable, and more verbose logs add noise without structured measurement.

questions.scenario: Which action helps diagnose why an ECS task on Fargate cannot pull its container image?
options: Check the task's stopped reason and confirm the execution role has ECR pull permissions and network egress
Add more subnets to the cluster
questions.explain: Image pull failures appear in the stopped reason and are usually caused by a task execution role lacking ECR permissions or by no route to ECR — a missing NAT gateway or VPC endpoint in a private subnet. Memory and subnet count do not affect image pulls, and Container Insights adds metrics without explaining this failure.

questions.scenario: Which approach provides the clearest signal that an asynchronous workflow has stalled?
options: An alarm on the age of the oldest message or the workflow's execution duration
questions.explain: Age of the oldest message, or execution duration exceeding an expected bound, directly indicates work is not progressing. Total invocation counts can look healthy while a backlog grows, the status page reports AWS-wide incidents rather than your workflow, and IAM policies relate to permissions.

questions.scenario: Which CloudFront setting should be reviewed when dynamic content is being served stale to users?
options: The cache policy TTL and which headers, cookies and query strings form the cache key
questions.explain: Stale dynamic content usually means the TTL is too long or the cache key omits a value that distinguishes responses, so different users share one cached object. Price class controls which edge locations are used, certificates handle TLS, and storage class affects origin cost rather than caching behaviour.

questions.scenario: A developer must identify the most expensive contributor to a Lambda function's bill. Which combination is MOST useful?
options: Cost Explorer grouped by function tag, alongside Duration and Invocations metrics
questions.explain: Cost Explorer attributes spend by tag or service while Duration and Invocations reveal whether the driver is call volume or execution time, together pointing to the right optimisation. Credential reports cover security, Flow Logs cover network traffic, and S3 inventory lists objects.
